title: EMCO WinNC for FANUC 31i Mill — Programming Reference Index
source: EMCO WinNC for Fanuc 31i Mill EN 1846 C 02
note: Original concise study notes keyed to manual PDF pages (PDF page numbering). This is not the full manual and is not a substitute for machine-specific documentation.

entries.guidance: Rapid travel is non-cutting positioning. Confirm clearance and tool approach before cutting moves.
Linear feed movement uses programmed axes and feed rate; check modal motion and coordinate positions.
Check clockwise or counterclockwise direction, active plane, end point and arc center/radius definition.
G17 selects XY, G18 selects ZX, and G19 selects YZ; check plane-dependent arcs and offsets.
G20 selects inches and G21 selects metric input; CNC Studio course examples use metric.
G41 is left and G42 right cutter compensation relative to feed direction; G40 cancels. Lead-in/out geometry matters.
G43 applies positive tool length offset with H; G44 negative, G49 cancels. Verify the tool length register.
G52 defines a local offset, G53 refers to machine coordinates for its block, and G54–G59 select work offsets.
G68 rotates the active coordinate system around a programmed center; G69 cancels.
Check Z, R, Q peck increment, P dwell, F feed and G98/G99 return mode.
Tapping behavior depends on controller and spindle synchronization; verify feed, pitch and cycle return settings.
Fine boring cycle with controller-dependent parameters; check axis and retract behavior.
G80 cancels active fixed drilling and boring cycles; confirm subsequent movements are not unintentionally cycled.
G81 drills to depth and rapidly retracts; G82 includes a dwell. Verify Z, R, F and return mode.
G83 retracts between pecks for chip removal; check Q, R, Z and F.
G85 feeds during drilling and withdrawal; G89 adds a dwell.
G90 programs absolute positions; G91 programs incremental displacements. Check modal state.
G94 is feed per minute; G95 is feed per spindle revolution. Interpret F accordingly.
G98 and G99 specify return to initial plane or R plane during canned cycles.
Machine program stop/end, spindle direction, tool change, and coolant functions. Machine-specific options may differ.
M29 tapping synchronization is machine/controller dependent; confirm it is supported by the chosen configuration.
M98 calls a subroutine with P program reference; M99 returns to the caller. Check target O numbers and repetition syntax.
